content: Google DeepMind ships Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash with 4K video and scene extension — AI Chat Daily ... Google DeepMind ships Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash with 4K video and scene extension ... The Omni update pushes generative video to 4K, extends clips to 40 seconds, and cuts draft costs to a third at 360p. ... Google DeepMind released Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash today, a production-ready update to its generative video model that adds 4K upscaling, scene extension up to 40 seconds, and first-and-last-frame interpolation. The model is live through the Gemini API in Google AI Studio and the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, and Adobe, Figma, and GMI Cloud are already shipping it inside production tools. The update is aimed squarely at developers building video workflows, not at consumer prompt-and-pray toys. ... The headline additions are control features that generative video has been missing. Scene extension now works in 10-second increments up to a cumulative 40 seconds, with the model analyzing 10 seconds of prior context to keep characters, lighting, and camera motion consistent. That is a step change from earlier Omni releases, which referenced only the final second of a clip before generating what came next. ... now specify a starting frame ... an ending frame ... them. Google Deep ... - 01Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash extends generated scenes up to a cumulative 40 seconds, in 10-second increments. - 02The model can now reason over 10 seconds of prior context, up from the final second in earlier versions. - 03360p drafts generate up to faster and cost a third of standard 720p output. - 04Final output can be upscaled to 1080p or 4K, with video references up to three seconds long. - 05Adobe Firefly, Figma Weave, and GMI Cloud are already shipping the model in production. ... The economics matter as much as the controls. Omni 1.1 Flash can generate 360p previews up to faster than 720p output and at roughly a third of the cost, which turns iteration from an expensive gamble into cheap scouting. Once a draft is approved, the same model upscales to 1080p or 4K for finishing. That two-tier pattern — cheap drafts, expensive finals — has been standard in film pipelines for decades, and Google DeepMind is finally bringing it to generative video. ... Adobe has integrated the model into Firefly for video editing, and Figma Weave is using it as one of the core generators on its canvas. GMI Cloud is running it through the Agent Platform API for production customers. Product managers Anish Nangia and Alisa Fortin, who authored the announcement, framed the release as the point at which Omni crosses from demo to deployment.

title: Google DeepMind Ran History's First AI Benchmark Evaluation Where Neither Side Could Cheat
summary: Google DeepMind Ran History's First AI Benchmark Evaluation Where Neither Side Could Cheat Deepmind.google For years, the AI evaluation industry had one structural problem no contractual safeguard could solve: whoever runs the test either has to hand the model provider the questions, or hand the e
content: Google DeepMind Ran History's First AI Benchmark Evaluation Where Neither Side Could Cheat ... For years, the AI evaluation industry had one structural problem no contractual safeguard could solve: whoever runs the test either has to hand the model provider the questions, or hand the evaluator the model. On August 27, 2026, Google DeepMind announced the world's first double-blind evaluation of a proprietary frontier-class AI model — one that required neither compromise, using cryptographic hardware to seal Gemini's weights and an external evaluator's benchmark prompts simultaneously inside a single hardware-encrypted enclave where neither party could see the other's protected data. ... The pilot, conducted in partnership with Singapore's AI Safety Institute (AISI), privacy-computing nonprofit OpenMined, AI benchmarking consortium MLCommons, and evaluation firm AVERI, tested Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite against confidential benchmarks — and its significance has nothing to do with how Gemini scored. What matters is how the test was run: for the first time in the industry's history, a model provider and an independent evaluator conducted a formal evaluation without either side needing to trust the other's word about what data they had seen. ... The most consequential implication of this pilot ... For now, the pilot stands as the first production-level proof that the adversarial trust problem at the center of AI benchmarking can be made architecturally irrelevant — not by improving procedures, but by removing the attack surface those procedures were trying to protect. ... Not automatically, and not universally. This pilot addresses one specific failure mode — the ability of a model provider to see evaluation prompts before or during a test, and the reciprocal risk of an evaluator seeing proprietary model weights. It does not address benchmark quality, benchmark management after the evaluation, or the question of whether the benchmark itself is well-designed and resistant to other forms of gaming. MLCommons explicitly noted that benchmark quality still requires careful management regardless of how well the prompts are protected during evaluation. And the pilot is currently limited to models that fit on a single NVIDIA H100 GPU, which excludes the largest frontier systems. What this pilot does provide is a mechanism: for the first time, an independent organization can evaluate a proprietary model against confidential benchmarks and produce results that neither side could have seen in advance — which is the necessary precondition for trustworthy evaluation, even if it is not sufficient on its own.

summary: Piloting the world's first double-blind AI evaluations — Google DeepMind August 27, 2026 Responsibility & Safety Piloting the world's first double-blind AI evaluations William Isaac, Sol Messing and Kristian Lum Share Building trust in proprietary model benchmarks using cryptographically secu
content: Piloting the world's first double-blind AI evaluations — Google DeepMind ... Responsibility & Safety ... Piloting the world's first double-blind AI evaluations ... Today, we’re introducing the world’s first double-blind evaluation of a proprietary, frontier class AI model, which keeps external evaluations confined to a cryptographic “box” where they can’t be used by models later to optimize performance ahead of testing. We're partnering with the Singapore AI Safety Institute, OpenMined, AVERI, and MLCommons, to test a Gemini Flash Lite model against confidential benchmarks in a privacy-preserving environment, increasing evaluation integrity. ... Double-blind evaluations eliminate this compromise. By using Confidential Space within Google Cloud’s Confidential Computing portfolio, we can cryptographically verify that both the external evaluation data and the proprietary model remain private to their respective owners. The evaluator cannot see the Gemini model weights, and Google cannot see the evaluator’s test prompts. ... We hope this pilot establishes a new frontier for model oversight, helping the broader industry build safer, more reliable, and widely trusted AI systems. To learn more about our methodology and findings, read our technical report.

content: Nvidia Acquires Hugging Face in $12.9 Billion Deal Reshaping AI - QUE.com ... Nvidia Acquires Hugging Face in $12.9 Billion Deal Reshaping AI ... In what may prove to be one of the most consequential acquisitions in the artificial intelligence industry’s young history, Nvidia has agreed to purchase Hugging Face for approximately $12.9 billion, according to multiple reports that broke in late August 2026. The deal, which values the open-source AI platform at nearly triple its last known valuation, signals a dramatic shift in how the world’s dominant AI chipmaker plans to cement its position in the rapidly evolving AI ecosystem. ... The Information first reported that Nvidia had reached an agreement to acquire Hugging Face for $12.9 billion, citing a source familiar with the matter. Business Insider, which initially broke the news over the prior weekend that Hugging Face was fielding takeover interest, noted that the talks — valuing the company at more than $13 billion — had not yet produced a signed agreement and could still fall apart. Reuters and CNBC independently confirmed the reporting, sending ripples through financial markets and the AI community alike. ... The $12.9 billion price tag represents a staggering jump from Hugging Face’s last known valuation. In 2023, the company raised $235 million in a funding round that valued it at $4.5 billion. That round was led by Salesforce Ventures, with additional investment from Alphabet’s GV, IBM Ventures, and notably, Nvidia itself. The acquisition price represents nearly a threefold increase in the company’s value in just three years — a testament to the explosive growth of the AI sector and Hugging Face’s central role within it. ... a $50 ... $7 billion ... a dominant investor that ... - Investment signal: The valuation jump from $4.5 billion to $12.9 billion in three years sends a powerful signal to investors and entrepreneurs about where value is being created in the AI ecosystem. Open-source AI platforms may become increasingly attractive acquisition targets. ... Finally, the deal must still close. Reports indicate that as of the announcement, the talks had not yet produced a signed agreement and could still unravel. In the fast-moving world of AI acquisitions, nothing is certain until the ink is dry. ... As the details continue to unfold, one thing is clear: the AI arms race is no longer just about who has the best models or the fastest chips. It is about who controls the ecosystem that connects them — and Nvidia just made a $12.9 billion bet that it will be that company.
